review: Independent one-time review of this expanded 22-step revision; every step read against the published-examples bar, stored doc-examples.json and vendored OpenAPI. No execution, pack edits, or reliance on the prior examples verdict.

rulings.rule: The published example must exercise its documented answer shape; setup steps make an example precondition true or read back its effect, and nothing else. An empty answer hides its item shape.
rulings.reason: Step 5 carries getEdgeConfigItems#doc example but intentionally returns an empty list before any mutation. Its vendor example contains a GlobalConfigItem with createdAt, description, edgeConfigId, key, updatedAt and value. The populated response is only requested by step 7, which lacks the example marker, so the example replay never checks that nonempty item schema. Step 5 also changes no precondition: the setup already supplied an empty config and the create request in step 6 establishes the needed item.
rulings.requiredChange: Delete step 5. Add example: getEdgeConfigItems#doc example to existing step 7, keeping its populated-item assertions and collection closure (path 1 exists false). That step then both replays the published GET against its nonempty precondition and reads back the canonical PATCH effect. Do not change the published PATCH request in step 6.

doubts.reason: The list schema patch rests on text saying list while the vendored schema renders an object. The inconsistency is explicitly recorded by exampleDiffers and supported by stored source quotes, so I do not rule it a hidden twin defect.

serviceType=zeit.world is asserted after zone=true without a registrar nameserver change. The request schema describes zone as an intention to use Vercel nameservers, while the response documents serviceType in terms of who handles DNS. Stored evidence does not conclusively state whether enabling the zone alone changes this field, so this remains a doubt rather than a contradiction.

The published request includes deprecated renew and customNameservers. The operation text explicitly says it is no longer used to update those fields, so replaying the published payload without asserting those deprecated effects is justified; an explicit undecided annotation would make that rationale easier to inspect.

The config list asserts its sole expected member's identity and zero item count but does not explicitly close the collection against additional configs. This is weaker assurance, not sufficient evidence of an incorrect example.

checked: All 22 steps and all 13 explicit example markers read.
Canonical PATCH body equals the stored page input, including operation=create, key=string, value=value, description=string.
Step 7 asserts every request-decided item field and the captured config ID, and closes the list.
Team/project/token/config setup establishes the used identity and resources; credentials are explicit on API requests.
Domain challenge name and value are captured and supplied through the external DNS door before verification.
Domain examples assert input/captured names, apex, project, redirect, redirectStatusCode and gitBranch and appropriate verification state.
Thin mutation replies have effect checks: canonical item write, zone update, project-domain removal and apex removal.
Read-back setup steps are authorized by the published-examples bar and are not judged as unnecessary customer-life reads.
getProjects response-envelope difference names a documented oneOf alternative; patchDomain difference names the update rather than move-out alternative.
Optional customEnvironmentId omission is explained by the absence of a custom environment in setup.
Vendor-assigned IDs and challenge values are captured rather than guessed; stagingPrefix is separately undecided.
